fullPassage: Resilience: The Power to Overcome City Wellness Center Newsletter This week’s topic in the City Wellness Center Newsletter is resilience, or “the power to overcome.” Julia Hone, a famous doctor, tells us how we can deal with difficult times by cultivating our inner strength. No life is free from problems. Whatever life path we choose, we all experience adversity. This can take the form of illness, accidents, failure in exams, family and relationship issues, or other stresses. To cope, we all need the ability to overcome difficulties, which is known as resilience. Resilience means springing back, just like a bouncy ball after hitting the ground. If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times you experience. Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity. So, resilience is the ability to handle, recover from, and benefit from difficult life events. There are countless stories of successful people who not only survived adversity but used it as a stepping stone to growth. Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories. “The hardship was a real blessing that inspired me to write stories like The Little Match Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling.” Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an opportunity. She was born with a medical condition that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee to surgery. She competed against athletes without disabilities in a national competition and participated in the Paralympics in 1996. Her career also includes modeling, acting, and public speaking. She says her physical condition is not a disability but the very thing that opened the door for her amazing potential. Both people succeeded not “despite” adversity but thanks to it. This is the real bouncing back. You might think “Hey, these are exceptional people.” However, we are all born with the potential for resilience. Just like these people, we all can develop the strength to quickly recover from a crisis that could otherwise cause lasting damage to our mental health. The good news is that resilience is like a muscle. You can build it up through practice, by developing thoughts, behaviors, and habits that allow you to recover from painful or stressful events. Here are three basic strategies to build up this “resilience muscle.” Three Basic Strategies to Build Up Your “Resilience Muscle” First, accept and respect adversity as a natural part of life. This doesn’t mean being passive, but understanding that some changes in life can cause suffering or stress. Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, “Why me?”, you can face whatever happens and focus on what you can change, not what you can’t. Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you confront them as a learning process. Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without adversity! Second, have “me time,” that is, personal time to look after yourself. Take a break and be in the present moment, neither regretting the past nor worrying about the future. Walk, meditate, write, draw, listen to music, or exercise. If you don’t know where to start, the STOP technique can be a great meditative technique. It works like this. Stop whatever you are doing. Take a few deep breaths. Observe your emotions and thoughts as they are, not judging them as good or bad. Proceed with what you were doing. Or start something different based on what you observed. Now go forward with your life. Third, be connected. Allow yourself to ask for help from people whom you can trust, such as friends, family members, or counselors. Talking about your issues with someone can help you see your situation with more clarity and respond to it with more strength. Good communication helps resilience. This is the reason why resilient people tend to create good support networks. I am not saying that these strategies are easy or remove all stress and suffering. Still, I urge you to practice them whenever you can, particularly when you are under stress. Remember that there is no better time to build your “resilience muscle” than the moment when you are in the middle of adversity and uncertainty. Practicing resilience during tough times helps you endure and grow stronger. However, you can also apply these strategies to everyday small stresses or minor challenges. Then you will gradually become more able to deal with big ones. Resilient people tend to be happier and more fulfilled because they are less afraid of failing or challenges. So, building resilience is the key not only to overcoming adversity but also to living a happy life.

questions.passage: To (A)[cope / panic], we all need the ability to overcome difficulties, which is known as resilience. Resilience means springing back, just like a bouncy ball after hitting the ground. If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times you experience. Furthermore, you learn and (B)[shrink / grow] from adversity. So, resilience is the ability to handle, recover from, and (C)[benefit / suffer] from difficult life events.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① cope(대처하다)+grow(성장하다)+benefit(이득을 얻다) ← 정답: 대처하기 위해 어려움을 극복하는 능력이 필요하고, 역경에서 배우고 성장하며 이득을 얻는다
❌ ② panic(당황하다)은 어려움에 대처한다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ③ shrink(위축되다), suffer(고통받다)는 성장하고 이득을 얻는다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ 3개 모두 문맥과 반대

questions.passage: There are countless stories of successful people who not only survived adversity but used it as a stepping stone to growth. Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood (A)[poverty / wealth], the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories. “The (B)[comfort / hardship] was a real blessing that inspired me to write stories like The Little Match Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling. ” Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an (C)[opportunity / obstacle].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① wealth(부)는 안데르센의 어린 시절 가난이라는 문맥과 반대
✅ ② poverty(가난)+hardship(고난)+opportunity(기회) ← 정답: 안데르센은 가난 등 고난이 작품의 원천이었고, Aimee Mullins는 시련을 기회로 보았다
❌ ③ comfort(안락), obstacle(장애물)은 고난이 축복이었고 시련을 기회로 봤다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ 3개 모두 문맥과 반대

questions.passage: ” Three Basic Strategies to Build Up Your “Resilience Muscle” First, accept and respect adversity as a (A)[natural / strange] part of life. This doesn’t mean being passive, but understanding that some changes in life can cause suffering or stress. Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, “Why me? ”, you can (B)[ignore / face] whatever happens and focus on what you can change, not what you can’t. Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you (C)[confront / escape] them as a learning process.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① strange(이상한), ignore(무시하다), escape(도망치다)는 모두 문맥과 반대
❌ ② ignore(무시하다)는 일어나는 일을 마주한다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ③ strange(이상한), escape(도망치다)는 역경을 삶의 자연스러운 일부로 받아들이라는 문맥과 반대
✅ ④ natural(자연스러운)+face(마주하다)+confront(맞서다) ← 정답: 역경을 삶의 자연스러운 일부로 받아들이고, 무슨 일이 일어나든 마주하며, 배움의 과정으로 맞서라

det.korean: ③ slowly → quickly: 회복탄력성이 있으면 힘든 시기에서 빠르게(quickly) 회복한다
det.analysis:
✅ ① problems: 문제로부터 자유로운 삶은 없다 적절
✅ ② illness: 역경이 질병의 형태를 띨 수 있다 적절
❌ ③ slowly(느리게) → quickly(빠르게) ← 정답: 공처럼 다시 튀어오르듯 빠르게 회복하는 것이 회복탄력성
✅ ④ hard: 힘든 시기 적절
det.tip: quickly(빠르게) ↔ slowly(느리게). bounce back = 빠른 회복

det.korean: ④ closed → opened: 그녀의 신체 조건은 놀라운 잠재력의 문을 열어 준(opened) 것이다
det.analysis:

✅ ③ includes: 경력에 모델·연기·대중 연설이 포함된다 적절

questions.passage: Third, be connected.  Allow yourself to ask for help from people whom you can ①<u>trust</u>, such as friends, family members, or counselors.  Talking about your issues with someone can help you see your situation with more ②<u>confusion</u> and respond to it with more strength.  Good communication helps resilience. det.korean: ② confusion → clarity: 누군가와 이야기하면 상황을 더 명료하게(clarity) 볼 수 있다
det.analysis:
✅ ① trust: 신뢰할 수 있는 사람들에게 도움을 청하라 적절
❌ ② confusion(혼란) → clarity(명료함) ← 정답: 대화는 상황을 더 명료하게 보고 더 강하게 대응하도록 돕는다
✅ ③ support: 좋은 지원망을 만든다 적절

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① muscle: 근육 ← 정답: 바로 뒤에서 연습을 통해 길러낼(build it up) 수 있다고 했으므로 근육 비유가 적절
❌ ② mirror: 거울 — 길러낸다는 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ burden: 짐 — 긍정적 능력이라는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ mystery: 수수께끼 — 연습으로 기른다는 문맥과 무관
det.tip: resilience is like a muscle: 회복탄력성은 근육처럼 연습으로 키울 수 있다

questions.passage: Second, have “me time,” that is, personal time to look after yourself.  Take a break and be in the __________ moment, neither regretting the past nor worrying about the future. det.analysis:
❌ ① past: 과거 — 과거를 후회하지 말라고 했으므로 부적합
❌ ② future: 미래 — 미래를 걱정하지 말라고 했으므로 부적합
✅ ③ present: 현재의 ← 정답: 과거 후회도 미래 걱정도 말고 현재 순간에 머물라
❌ ④ distant: 먼 — 문맥상 어색함
det.tip: be in the present moment: 과거(regretting the past)도 미래(worrying about the future)도 아닌 현재 순간에 머물기

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① endure: 견디다 ← 정답: 힘든 시기에 회복탄력성을 연습하면 견디고 더 강하게 성장하도록 돕는다
❌ ② escape: 도망치다 — 역경에 맞선다는 글 전체 흐름과 반대
❌ ③ complain: 불평하다 — 문맥상 어색함
❌ ④ celebrate: 축하하다 — 힘든 시기라는 문맥과 무관
det.tip: helps you endure and grow stronger: 견디고 더 강하게 성장하도록 돕는다

questions.passage: No life is free from problems.  Whatever life path we choose, we all experience <u>adversity</u>.  This can take the form of illness, accidents, failure in exams, family and relationship issues, or other stresses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 adversity와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① prosperity: 번영 — 의미가 반대
✅ ② hardship: 고난 — adversity(역경)와 같은 뜻이므로 정답
❌ ③ comfort: 안락 — 의미가 반대
❌ ④ leisure: 여가 — 의미가 다름

questions.passage: There are <u>countless</u> stories of successful people who not only survived adversity but used it as a stepping stone to growth.  Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories.  “The hardship was a real blessing that inspired me to write stories like The Little Match Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 countless와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① limited: 제한된 — 의미가 반대
❌ ② ancient: 고대의 — 의미가 다름
❌ ③ valuable: 귀중한 — 의미가 다름
✅ ④ numerous: 수많은 — countless(셀 수 없이 많은)와 같은 뜻이므로 정답
det.tip: countless = numerous = 수많은, 셀 수 없이 많은

det.analysis:
✅ ① barriers: 장벽 — obstacles(장애물)와 같은 뜻이므로 정답
❌ ② rewards: 보상 — 의미가 다름
❌ ③ solutions: 해결책 — 의미가 다름
❌ ④ memories: 기억 — 의미가 다름

questions.passage: She says her physical condition is not a disability but the very thing that opened the door for her amazing potential.  Both people succeeded not “despite” adversity but thanks to it.  This is the real bouncing back.  You might think “Hey, these are <u>exceptional</u> people.

det.analysis:
❌ ① remarkable: 놀랄 만한 (오히려 유의어)
✅ ② ordinary: 평범한 ← 정답: exceptional(특출난)과 정반대
❌ ③ wealthy: 부유한 — 의미축이 다름

det.analysis:

❌ ② frequent: 빈번한 — 의미축이 다름
✅ ③ significant: 중대한 ← 정답: minor(사소한)와 정반대
❌ ④ sudden: 갑작스러운 — 의미축이 다름

questions.passage:
(A) She was born with a medical <u>condition</u> that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee to surgery. However, she grew up to compete as a successful athlete.
(B) You can borrow my laptop on one <u>condition</u>: you must return it by tomorrow morning. I need it for my class presentation.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 condition의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① (A)와 (B)의 의미가 뒤바뀌어 있음
✅ ② (A) medical condition = 질환, (건강) 상태 / (B) on one condition = 한 가지 조건 ← 정답
❌ ③ (B)는 환경이 아니라 조건(빌려주는 전제)
❌ ④ (A)는 환경이 아니라 건강 상태

다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a natural ability or quality that could develop in the future and lead to success"

det.analysis:
❌ ① tradition: 전통 — 정의와 무관
❌ ② emotion: 감정 — 정의와 무관
❌ ③ sacrifice: 희생 — 정의와 무관

det.tip: potential = 잠재력 (the potential for resilience: 회복탄력성의 잠재력은 누구에게나 있다)

questions.passage: Julia Hone, a famous doctor, tells us how we can deal with difficult times by __________ (cultivate) our inner strength. No life is free from problems. Whatever life path we choose, we all experience adversity.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: cultivate(동사 원형) → cultivating(동명사): 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 써야 한다. 'by cultivating our inner strength'는 '내면의 힘을 기름으로써'라는 뜻

questions.passage: Stop whatever you are doing. Take a few deep breaths. Observe your emotions and thoughts as they are, not __________ (judge) them as good or bad. Proceed with what you were doing.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: judge(동사 원형) → judging(현재분사): 'not judging them as good or bad'는 분사구문의 부정형으로, 'Observe ~'와 동시에 일어나는 동작을 나타낸다. 분사구문의 부정은 not을 분사 앞에 둔다. '좋고 나쁨을 판단하지 않으면서 관찰하라'는 뜻
det.tip: 분사구문 부정: not + 현재분사(-ing) → not judging

det.analysis:
✅ ① support networks: 지원망 ← 정답: 신뢰하는 사람들에게 도움을 청하고 좋은 소통이 회복탄력성을 돕기에, 회복탄력적인 사람들은 좋은 지원망을 만든다
❌ ② strict schedules: 엄격한 일정 — 소통·연결이라는 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ financial assets: 금융 자산 — 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ private spaces: 사적인 공간 — 사람들과 연결되라는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: create good support networks: 좋은 지원망을 만들다 (be connected와 연결)
